name: SoFi Technologies, Inc.
moat_justification: Real, compounding advantages — a national bank charter with a $45.5B deposit base (Q2 2026), a 15.8M-member cross-sell loop (24.4M products, +42% YoY; existing members opened 51% of new products in Q2 2026), and the Galileo/Technisys B2B infrastructure arm — but the consumer products are commodities contested by JPMorgan, Capital One, Chime, Robinhood and every large-bank app, deposits must be bought with a competitive APY, Technology Platform revenue declined YoY in Q2 2026, and the core asset is unsecured consumer credit whose returns are set by the credit cycle. No pricing power has been demonstrated through a downturn. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years (moot here — no positive OE base).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 11.6%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Digital bank/fintech, moat 5/10 — GAAP-profitable and compounding fast (Q2 2026 revenue +43% YoY, 15.8M members), but conservative owner's earnings are negative on every filing basis (normalized -$3.39/sh, TTM -$6.65/sh) because a growing lender's OCF is consumed by loan-book growth; the OE DCF cannot support $15.09 — Tier F, low confidence on sector-model mismatch.
moat_for: National bank charter (2022) and deposit funding — $45.5B of deposits at Q2 2026 funding the loan book, replacing costlier warehouse funding
Member ecosystem / cross-sell loop — 15.8M members (+35% YoY), 24.4M products (+42%), existing members opened 51% of new products in Q2 2026
Technology Platform (Galileo + Technisys / SoFi Tech Solutions) — B2B payment processing, card issuing and core-banking infrastructure sold to third parties
Scale and brand in digital consumer finance — record $14.8B of originations in Q2 2026 across personal, student and home loans to a high-income member base
moat_against: Commodity products, no proven pricing power — loans, deposits, investing and cards contested by the largest banks and fintechs
Deposit advantage must be bought with rate — funding edge narrows when competitors match its savings APY
Earnings geared to unsecured consumer credit — personal-loan charge-offs are the swing factor and the book is untested at scale in a recession
Technology Platform momentum stalled — segment revenue declined YoY in Q2 2026; Galileo competes with Marqeta and in-house bank builds
Dilution and capital retention — share count +11.6%/yr (engine); a growing bank must retain capital against its loan book, limiting distributable cash
